original_query: SELECT t5.ENAME FROM (SELECT ENAME, JOB FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A' GROUP BY ENAME, JOB) AS t5 LEFT JOIN (SELECT NAME FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME) AS t6 ON t5.JOB = t6.NAME GROUP BY t5.ENAME

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Removed the derived table t5 (GROUP BY ENAME, JOB) since the outer query only groups by ENAME; grouping by JOB is redundant and is collapsed into a single DISTINCT.

Removed the LEFT JOIN to t6 (distinct DEPT.NAME). The join output is unused in the SELECT list, the LEFT JOIN cannot filter rows, and the outer GROUP BY t5.ENAME collapses any join effects, so the DEPT table is entirely irrelevant.
The final result is exactly the distinct ENAME values satisfying ENAME = 'A'; the multiple nested GROUP BY levels are replaced by a single DISTINCT on the filtered EMP scan.

Recommended creating an index on EMP(ENAME) (e.g., CREATE INDEX ON EMP (ENAME)) since EMP has 45M rows; this enables an index-only scan for the filtered column, avoiding the current costly parallel sequential scan.
